title: Singleness and Devotion
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Singleness and devotion teaches that singleness is not a lesser life, failed life, or incomplete life. It can be a faithful calling in which a believer serves Christ with focused devotion, contentment, and fruitfulness.
summary: Singleness and devotion teaches that singleness is not a lesser life, failed life, or incomplete life. It can be a faithful calling in which a believer serves Christ with focused devotion, contentment, and fruitfulness.
christFocus: Jesus Christ gives ultimate identity and belonging to every believer, married or unmarried. In Him, singleness can be lived with dignity, purpose, holiness, and undivided devotion to the Lord.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture honors marriage, but it also honors singleness. Paul speaks of singleness as a gift that can allow undivided attention to the things of the Lord.

Singleness is not spiritual second class. Jesus Himself lived unmarried, and His life was perfectly full, holy, fruitful, and pleasing to the Father.

For some, singleness is a season; for others, it may be lifelong. In either case, believers are called to holiness, contentment, fellowship, service, and devotion to Christ.

The church must not treat unmarried believers as incomplete or invisible. In Christ, every believer belongs to the family of God and has meaningful purpose in the body.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many singles feel overlooked, pressured, or defined by what they do not have. This doctrine speaks dignity and purpose: life is complete in Christ, not in marital status.

It also challenges the church to honor and include singles fully in discipleship, ministry, hospitality, friendship, and spiritual family.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Live your current calling before Christ with faithfulness. If single, do not believe your life is on hold. Seek holiness, service, deep fellowship, and devotion to the Lord. If married, honor singles as full members of Christ’s body with gifts and purpose.
